title: indigo_agent_scheduler: replace the DEFER strength with a COMPACT / VISIBILITY strategy switch
description:
Owner report (2026-11-19, running server, DEFER = 100): tasks never get the better slot, they are moved to well before the meridian. Reproduced offline from the server's tasks (lat 42, lon 23, 2026-11-19): with DEFER 100 the plan is Soul 20:40, Pleiades 21:08 (transit 22:19), Jellyfish 21:29-23:30 (transit 00:49, 76 % of its transit altitude), Orion 23:30, Rosette 00:30, then nothing until the shutdown hook at 04:19.

Cause: decide() in indigo_agent_scheduler_plan.c weighs holding the best candidate alone against a greedy simulation in which every other task still starts as early as possible, so a hold only lets the next task into the slot and is rejected; holding the group is never evaluated. Every hold is also dropped when any run starts. The 0-100 DEFER strength (a threshold of a run-quality gain) is hard to understand.

Owner decision: keep the old greedy algorithm and replace the DEFER number with a switch between two preferences, instead of patching the deferral further.

Proposal (to be settled in the design stage):
- Replace AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS.DEFER with a switch property, e.g. AGENT_SCHEDULER_STRATEGY with items COMPACT (default, exactly the greedy plan and selection as before DEFER) and VISIBILITY (best visibility). Remove decide(), defer_release(), the holds, release_holds() and deferred_from logic, and the DEFER item and its docs.
- VISIBILITY: build the greedy plan, add the runs it left out wherever they still fit, then choose the order and start times that maximize the summed run quality (mean altitude in % of transit altitude) without dropping any run: exact dynamic programming of start times on a 1-minute grid for a given order (eligibility of the whole run, repeat spacing, start before the night end), local search over the order (move one run to another position) seeded with the greedy order and the order by best-quality time. Urgent tasks and running runs stay fixed; priority still decides which runs are in the plan. The scheduler starts the plan's first run at its planned time and replans after each run as now; REASON names the task and slot it waits for.
- Prototype in the session scratchpad (defer/b.c, b.h) measured on 1000 random nights (3-10 tasks, repeats, high priority) with replanning after every run: total quality +8.6 % against DEFER 100 (476.8k vs 439.1k), +2.9 % runs (5835 vs 5673), worse than DEFER on 17 nights with the same run count, fewer runs on 11 nights (5 against greedy; must become 0 by construction). On tonight's tasks: Pleiades 22:10 99.9 %, Orion 23:15 98 %, Jellyfish 23:46-01:47 98 %, Rosette 01:47 97 %, total 584 vs 558. Cost about 3 ms per decision on an i5 (re-measure worst case and on a Pi).
- Open design questions: names of the property/items; whether run quality is weighted by run duration (a 2 h run counts like a 20 min run in the prototype); guarantees (never fewer runs than the greedy plan, fallback to the greedy plan when the optimizer finds no feasible arrangement); behaviour with nightly windows and hooks (a run delays a hook, it does not overlap-block it); keeping the plan stable across replans.
- Update SCHEDULER.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (explain both modes well), PROPERTIES.md, indigo_names.h, tools/scheduler_sandbox.py, unit tests (plan) and integration tests; bump the driver version.

outcome.summary: Code, plan validity, COMPACT path, IDLE (Q5b), persistence, version 0x0300001D, Makefile/Xcode, formatting and tests are fine. Reviewer ran: unit test_agent_scheduler_plan/night/sky/header all passed; integration test_agent_scheduler 134/134 passed; bench_scheduler_plan 200 nights: 0 nights with fewer runs, 0 violations, max plan 34 ms. Only small documentation fixes are needed: (1) indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/doc/SCHEDULER.md:28: the INDIGO column of the comparison table still describes DEFER ('optional look-ahead that holds a task back for a slot nearer its culmination when no run is lost'). It should describe the COMPACT/VISIBILITY strategies. (2) SCHEDULER.md:656 says 'per task the plan has at least the runs of the COMPACT plan', and INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md:249 says 'The plan keeps every run that COMPACT would make'. Both contradict SCHEDULER.md:662 and the code at plan.c:1006 together with vis_better(), which compares only total runs. The previous-plan seed can replace a COMPACT run with an earlier promised run of the same or higher class. Example: the previous plan has A and B (normal), the new COMPACT plan has A and C (normal), and C fits nowhere next to A and B. Both candidates have 2 runs, and S1 wins on J or the tie, so C is not planned. Reword both places to 'never fewer runs in total, and no run of a higher class is dropped', or similar. The owner should acknowledge this deviation from design 2.3 item 7. (3) indigo_test/unit/test_agent_scheduler_night.c:101 has a stale comment: 'the scheduler keeps a deferral wait then' should say that a VISIBILITY plan is kept. Observations, no change needed: Q5(b) suppresses IDLE for any idle period under VISIBILITY when the next planned run is within IDLE_PARK_AFTER, including waits for a window (integration test visibility_short_wait_keeps_the_idle_hook); this matches the documentation. A pinned urgent run's eligibility at its rounded-up minute is not checked; it is a forecast only, because select_urgent() decid

Re-review of 9fda4f477 against f7234066b. The diff touches 5 files with 8 lines changed, all of them documentation or comments: INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (step 4, the VISIBILITY bullet and the 'What VISIBILITY respects' bullet), PROPERTIES.md (the AGENT_SCHEDULER_STRATEGY row), SCHEDULER.md (comparison table line 28 and constraint 6), the doc comment of indigo_scheduler_plan_visibility() in plan.h, and the comment at test_agent_scheduler_night.c:101. No code logic changed. All three earlier findings are fixed. The new wording is consistent and accurate against the code. The total run count is never below COMPACT, which the final check guarantees. A COMPACT run can be left out only by the previous-plan seed (plan.c:1006), never an urgent one and never one of a higher class: the code drops a run only when its class is at most the lowest class of the kept runs, which is stricter than the documented condition, so the docs do not overclaim. The earlier test results stand: unit plan/night/sky/header passed and the integration test passed 134/134. No retest was needed for these comment-only changes.

history.text:
Prototype tests of the open design questions (2026-11-19, scratchpad defer/v.c + v.h; 1000 random nights at lat 42 lon 23, 3-10 tasks, 25 % repeated twice every 60 min, 20 % high priority, replanning after every run; plus the owner's tasks of 2026-11-19).

How VISIBILITY works in the prototype: (1) greedy plan as COMPACT decides which runs; (2) runs greedy left out are inserted where they fit best; (3) for a given order, dynamic programming on a 1-minute grid picks the start times that maximize summed run quality (each run eligible over its whole length, repeat spacing, start before night end; runs may delay hooks, as in the scheduler); (4) local search moves one run to another position, seeded with the greedy order, the order by best-quality time and the rest of the previous plan; (5) the scheduler starts the first run at its planned time and replans after each run.

Results (runs / mean quality per run / time-weighted quality / nights with fewer runs than greedy / same-run nights worse than DEFER 100, time-weighted):
- greedy: 5595 / 68.8 % / 70.0 %
- DEFER 100 (current): 5673 / 77.4 % / 76.8 %
- VISIBILITY: 5836 / 81.7 % / 80.7 % / 5 / 21
- + run length weighting: 5827 / 80.9 % / 80.8 % / 9 / 18
- + previous plan as seed: 5844 / 81.8 % / 80.8 % / 0 / 18
- + both: 5839 / 80.9 % / 80.9 % / 0 / 12
Owner's tasks: all VISIBILITY variants 6 runs, mean 97.3 % (DEFER 100: 93.0 %, greedy 73.1 %); Jellyfish 23:46-01:47 at 98 % (transit 00:49).

Findings for the design:
1. Duration weighting changes little (+0.1 point time-weighted, -0.8 per run); recommended because it measures hours of data at good altitude.
2. Keeping the rest of the previous plan as a seed (kept unless strictly better or more runs) removed every night with fewer runs than greedy. Remaining gap: about 2 % of decisions (120 of ~5800) found no arrangement and fell back to the greedy step, all with repeated tasks whose runs are not adjacent in the order (repeat spacing across other runs); the prototype's DP
